definition: Text normalization is the process of transforming text into a single canonical form that it might not have had before.
details: Normalizing text before storing or processing it allows for separation of concerns, since input is guaranteed to be consistent before operations are performed on it. Text normalization requires being aware of what type of text is to be normalized and how it is to be processed afterwards; there is no all-purpose normalization procedure.

explainer.lead: Text normalization transforms text into a single canonical form it may not have had, so downstream processing sees consistent input. It matters because it separates concerns: input is guaranteed consistent before operations run on it.

tiers.eli5: It is like tidying a messy desk into one standard arrangement before you start working, so everything is in a predictable place.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers normalize text before storing or processing it so later steps can rely on a consistent format. The pitfall is that normalization depends on what type of text it is and how it will be processed afterward, so there is no all-purpose procedure and a choice that suits one pipeline can damage another.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally it is a function mapping a text string to a canonical representative of its equivalence class under some chosen criteria. There is no universal normalization function: the definition of "canonical" is task-specific and must be fixed in advance.

explainer.example: Before analysis, variant spellings and formats are rewritten to one chosen canonical form so that matching and comparison work reliably.
